messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 2222223333 — Elevated latency and errors on embeddings routes in us-west-2. Error rate +12% (5m), p95 latency spike. Paging @jess-oncall and @maya-sre.

jess-oncall: On it. Observed 502/503s for /v1/embeddings and timeouts when clients request long batch sizes. Any noisy tenants?

siva: early glance — large batched jobs from a single API key spiking token usage. Top offenders: key:acct-7fX and acct-1Bz (embeddings-heavy). They're doing big bulk embeddings (batch sizes ~512).

maya-sre: Can we do per-route shaping first (embeddings) before global throttles? Prefer per-endpoint to avoid impacting chat SLA.

jess-oncall: Agreed. Proposed quick mitigations: 1) Apply route-specific RPS and concurrency caps for /embeddings 2) Rate-limit large batch sizes 3) Disable rerank for public/free tier as it uses costly rerank infra. Thoughts?

leo-eng: +1. We have runtime knobs exposed in admin CLI. I can apply a temporary quota policy. Example:
```bash
# throttle embeddings to 40 reqs/s per customer, 60s window
rwdctl quota set --route /v1/embeddings --per-customer 40 --window 60s --reason "mitigate noisy bulk embeddings"

# limit batch size to 128 for public tier
rwdctl config set --route /v1/embeddings --param max_batch_size=128 --scope public --reason "protect cluster"

# disable rerank for free tier
rwdctl quota set --route /v1/rerank --scope free --limit 0 --reason "temporary disable rerank to free capacity"
```

jess-oncall: Do it. Also set a higher priority for chat routes so they bypass embeddings shaping if feasible.

leo-eng: Applying now. Pushing one-off policy via admin-api, will post audit id.

deploy-bot: action:quota_update executed by leo-eng. audit_id: a2f9c3d0. Changes: {"/v1/embeddings":{"per_customer_rps":40,"max_batch_size_public":128},"/v1/rerank":{"free_tier":0}}

support-bot: Noted. Routing CS: @emily-cs — probable customer impact: accounts with heavy bulk embeddings may see queued or throttled requests; some may get 429.

emily-cs: Reaching out to top affected customers (acct-7fX, acct-1Bz). Triage message ready: "We're temporarily limiting bulk embeddings to preserve service for real-time endpoints; if you need a higher throughput please contact support for dedicated capacity." Will post and tag.

jess-oncall: Monitoring metrics now. p95 latency for chat unchanged so mitigation working. Embeddings error rate down from +12% to +3% after 2m.

maya-sre: One caveat — the per-customer RPS enforcement is implemented at the service edge; large in-flight KV cache writes still can spike memory. Recommend also enabling small-prefetch-cap reduction for embeddings workers temporarily.

leo-eng: Turning on reduced prefetch on embeddings worker pool:
```json
{
  "worker_pool":"embeddings-usw2",
  "prefetch_window":50,
  "reason":"reduce memory pressure during noisy bulk jobs",
  "expires_in":"30m"
}
```

deploy-bot: action:worker_config applied by leo-eng. audit_id: b4d7e1a9.

support-bot: Received initial customer replies — 2 customers acknowledged, one asked for ETA. Emily sent targeted note with alternative: dedicated batch window on Dedicated clusters.

jess-oncall: Handing incident to maya-sre for follow-up and rollback plan in 30m. @maya-sre you own postmortem if we need one. I'll stay available for escalations.

maya-sre: Taking over. Plan: keep current quotas for 30 min, observe error rates and queue length. If stable, rollback batch_size public to 256 and reduce per-customer RPS to a higher baseline (60 rps) during low traffic window. Also collect example traces from affected customers for postmortem.

jess-oncall: Add TODOs to runbook: list affected API keys, duration of throttle, audit ids (a2f9c3d0, b4d7e1a9), and exact CLI commands used.

leo-eng: Adding runbook entries and the exact JSON snippets under incident folder.

maya-sre: Update: metrics stable at T+14m. Embeddings error rate steady ~2.8%, total cluster token utilization down 18%. Leaving shaping on. Will coordinate rollback window after 30m if no regressions.

jess-oncall: Status update to #incidents: embeddings mitigation applied, chat unaffected, support notified. Will post final resolution when rollback complete. :white_check_mark:

emily-cs: CS note posted to affected customers. One asked for ETA and requested temporary quota bump — instructing them to open a support ticket for expedited review.

maya-sre: Final update (T+32m): metrics remain stable. Rolling back max_batch_size_public -> 256 and per-customer RPS -> 60.

deploy-bot: action:quota_update executed by maya-sre. audit_id: c9e8f2b3. Changes rolled back: {"/v1/embeddings":{"per_customer_rps":60,"max_batch_size_public":256},"/v1/rerank":{"free_tier":0}}

jess-oncall: Closing the paging. Postmortem owner: @maya-sre. Follow-ups: long-term: auto-detect noisy bulk embeddings and suggest Dedicated, add per-tenant token budgeting alert, consider adaptive batch-size algorithm in runtime.

maya-sre: Acknowledged. I'll file the postmortem and include mitigation timeline + customer impact.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 2222223333 status: resolved. duration: 00:38:16.
